text: NEP 2020 replaces the 10+2 school structure with which curricular and pedagogical structure?
textHi: NEP 2020 ने 10+2 विद्यालय संरचना को किस पाठ्यचर्या एवं शैक्षणिक संरचना से प्रतिस्थापित किया है?

options.whyIncorrect: Not proposed by NEP 2020.
Incorrect ordering; the correct structure begins with a 5-year Foundational Stage.
This resembles the older elementary+secondary split, not NEP 2020.

explanation: 5+3+3+4 covers ages 3–18: Foundational Stage (3 yrs Anganwadi/pre-school + Classes 1–2; ages 3–8), Preparatory (Classes 3–5; ages 8–11), Middle (Classes 6–8; ages 11–14), Secondary (Classes 9–12; ages 14–18). PRTs teach in the Foundational and Preparatory stages.
examRelevance: Most-asked NEP 2020 fact; also a guaranteed KVS interview question.

text: The NIPUN Bharat Mission aims to ensure that every child attains foundational literacy and numeracy by the end of:
textHi: निपुण भारत मिशन का लक्ष्य है कि प्रत्येक बच्चा किसके अंत तक बुनियादी साक्षरता और संख्या-ज्ञान प्राप्त कर ले?

options.whyIncorrect: Class 5 marks the end of the Preparatory Stage, later than the FLN target.
Class 8 is the end of elementary education under RTE, not the FLN target.
Too early; FLN is a Grade 3 outcome.

explanation: NIPUN (National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy) Bharat was launched on 5 July 2021 under Samagra Shiksha. Its goal: universal FLN by the end of Grade 3 by 2026-27, with Lakshya (targets) for each grade from Balvatika to Class 3.
source: NIPUN Bharat Guidelines, Ministry of Education (2021)
examRelevance: FLN/NIPUN is the single most important 'new initiative' topic for primary teacher exams.

text: Which of the following is an example of FORMATIVE assessment?
textHi: निम्न में से कौन रचनात्मक (formative) मूल्यांकन का उदाहरण है?

options.text: Annual examination at the end of the session
options.whyIncorrect: Year-end exams are summative — they judge learning after instruction ends.
Board exams are large-scale summative assessments.

options.text: Teacher observing group work and giving feedback during the lesson to adjust teaching
Ranking students by marks for the merit list
options.whyIncorrect: Ranking is a summative, norm-referenced use of results.

explanation: Formative assessment (assessment FOR learning) happens during instruction to give feedback and modify teaching; summative assessment (assessment OF learning) happens at the end to certify achievement. NEP 2020 shifts assessment towards regular, formative, competency-based methods.
examRelevance: Formative vs summative distinction is asked almost every year.

text: A test measures what it claims to measure. This property is called:
textHi: एक परीक्षण वही मापता है जिसे मापने का वह दावा करता है। इस गुण को क्या कहते हैं?

options.whyIncorrect: Reliability is consistency of scores across time/forms, not accuracy of purpose.
Objectivity means scoring is free from the scorer's personal bias.
Usability concerns practicality — cost, time, ease of administration.

explanation: Validity = the test measures what it is intended to measure (content, construct, criterion validity). A test can be reliable without being valid, but cannot be valid without being reliable.
source: Educational Measurement — Gronlund; D.El.Ed. Evaluation unit
examRelevance: Characteristics of a good test — a direct syllabus item under 'measurement and evaluation'.

text: The 'Project Method' of teaching is associated with:
textHi: शिक्षण की 'प्रोजेक्ट विधि' किससे संबंधित है?

options.whyIncorrect: Montessori developed the Montessori method with didactic apparatus and sensory training.
Froebel founded the Kindergarten and used 'gifts and occupations'.
Spencer is known for the utilitarian/scientific curriculum, not the project method.

explanation: Kilpatrick (a student of John Dewey) formalised the Project Method: 'a whole-hearted purposeful activity proceeding in a social environment'. Steps: providing situation, choosing, planning, executing, evaluating, recording.

text: Micro-teaching, developed at Stanford University (Allen & Ryan), is best described as:
textHi: स्टैनफोर्ड विश्वविद्यालय (एलन और रयान) में विकसित सूक्ष्म-शिक्षण का सर्वोत्तम वर्णन है:

options.text: Teaching very young children in small groups
options.whyIncorrect: Micro-teaching is a teacher-training technique, not about the age of learners.

options.text: A scaled-down teaching encounter (small class, 5–10 min, one skill) with feedback and re-teach cycle

options.whyIncorrect: Unrelated to the term.
Micro-teaching predates online video and is about skill practice.

explanation: Micro-teaching cycle: Plan → Teach → Feedback → Re-plan → Re-teach → Re-feedback. It isolates skills like set induction, questioning, stimulus variation, reinforcement, explaining and blackboard writing.
source: Allen & Ryan, Micro-teaching (1969); Indian model by Passi
examRelevance: Teaching skills topic — micro-teaching steps and skills are frequently asked.

text: Herbart's steps of lesson planning, in the correct order, are:
textHi: हरबर्ट के पाठ योजना के पद सही क्रम में हैं:

options.whyIncorrect: Preparation (introduction) must come before presentation.
Generalisation cannot precede presentation of content.
Application is the final step after generalisation.

explanation: Herbartian five steps: Preparation/Introduction, Presentation, Comparison/Association, Generalisation, Application (a sixth, Recapitulation, is often added). Lesson plans in Indian teacher training largely follow this sequence.
examRelevance: Sequence questions on Herbartian steps appear regularly.

text: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 applies to children in which age group?
textHi: निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार (RTE) अधिनियम, 2009 किस आयु वर्ग के बच्चों पर लागू होता है?

options.whyIncorrect: 3–18 is the coverage NEP 2020 PROPOSES to extend RTE to, not the current Act.
Not the statutory age band.
0–6 is covered by ICDS/Anganwadi and Article 45 (ECCE), not RTE.

explanation: RTE Act 2009 (effective 1 April 2010) gives effect to Article 21-A: free and compulsory elementary education (Classes 1–8) for children aged 6–14. Key provisions: Section 12(1)(c) 25% EWS seats in private schools, no detention (amended 2019 to allow states to detain in Class 5 and 8 after re-exam), PTR norms, no corporal punishment (Sec. 17), no screening for admission.
examRelevance: RTE age group is a certain question; also useful for interview.

text: In early reading instruction, 'phonological awareness' refers to a child's ability to:
textHi: प्रारंभिक पठन शिक्षण में 'ध्वन्यात्मक जागरूकता' का अर्थ है बच्चे की यह क्षमता:

options.text: Recognise and manipulate the sounds of spoken language (syllables, rhymes, individual sounds)

options.whyIncorrect: That is handwriting/graphomotor skill.

options.text: Understand the meaning of a paragraph
options.whyIncorrect: That is reading comprehension.
Alphabet recitation is rote knowledge of letter names, not sound awareness.

explanation: Phonological awareness (including phonemic awareness) is an oral skill and a strong predictor of later reading success. It underpins decoding — mapping sounds (varna/akshara) to symbols. NIPUN Bharat's reading components: oral language, phonological awareness, decoding, vocabulary, fluency, comprehension, writing.
source: NIPUN Bharat Guidelines — components of FLN

text: Under the RTE Act 2009, the School Management Committee (SMC) must have at least what proportion of its members as parents/guardians of children in the school?
textHi: RTE अधिनियम 2009 के अंतर्गत विद्यालय प्रबंधन समिति (SMC) में विद्यालय के बच्चों के अभिभावकों का न्यूनतम अनुपात क्या होना चाहिए?

options.whyIncorrect: Too low; the Act requires a strong parent majority.
Half is required for WOMEN among the parent members, not for parents overall.
SMC also includes elected representatives, teachers and the head teacher.

explanation: Section 21 of RTE Act: SMC comprises elected local-authority representatives, parents/guardians and teachers; at least three-fourths must be parents/guardians, with proportionate representation of disadvantaged/weaker sections, and 50% of members women. SMC prepares the School Development Plan.
examRelevance: Educational management and administration — SMC composition is a frequent question in UP exams.

text: Which constitutional amendment inserted Article 21-A making education a fundamental right?
textHi: किस संविधान संशोधन ने अनुच्छेद 21-A जोड़कर शिक्षा को मौलिक अधिकार बनाया?

options.whyIncorrect: 42nd Amendment moved 'education' from the State List to the Concurrent List.
73rd Amendment relates to Panchayati Raj.
93rd Amendment enabled reservation for OBCs in educational institutions (Art. 15(5)).

explanation: The 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21-A (right to education for 6–14 years), amended Article 45 (ECCE for children below 6) and added fundamental duty 51-A(k) — parents to provide education opportunities to children aged 6–14.
examRelevance: Overlaps with 'Indian Constitution' topic in EVS/SST — high yield.

text: The NCF for the Foundational Stage (2022) recommends 'Panchaadi' — a five-step learning process. The correct sequence is:
textHi: NCF बुनियादी स्तर (2022) 'पंचाड़ी' — पाँच चरणों की अधिगम प्रक्रिया — की अनुशंसा करता है। सही क्रम है:

options.text: Aditi (introduction) → Bodh (conceptual understanding) → Abhyas (practice) → Prayog (application) → Prasar (expansion)

options.whyIncorrect: Practice cannot precede introduction and understanding.
Introduction (Aditi) comes first.
Understanding (Bodh) should precede practice (Abhyas).

explanation: NCF-FS 2022 describes Panchaadi: Aditi (introduction/engagement), Bodh (conceptual understanding), Abhyas (practice), Prayog (application), Prasar (expansion/extension). It is an example of play-based, experiential pedagogy for ages 3–8.
source: National Curriculum Framework for Foundational Stage 2022, Chapter on Pedagogy
examRelevance: NCF-FS 2022 is a recent policy document — expect new-initiative questions from it.

text: Which of these best reflects 'inclusive education' as understood in NEP 2020 and the RPwD Act?
textHi: NEP 2020 और RPwD अधिनियम में 'समावेशी शिक्षा' को कौन सबसे अच्छी तरह दर्शाता है?

options.text: Children with disabilities study in separate special classrooms within a regular school
options.whyIncorrect: This is 'integration' or segregated provision, not inclusion.

options.text: All children, regardless of disability, gender, caste or socio-economic background, learn together in the same classroom with the system adapting to their needs
Only children who can cope with the regular curriculum are admitted
options.whyIncorrect: Conditional admission is the opposite of inclusion.

options.text: Special schools for all children with disabilities
options.whyIncorrect: Special schools are a last resort; inclusion is the default.

explanation: RPwD Act 2016 Sec. 2(m) defines inclusive education as a system where students with and without disability learn together and the teaching–learning is suitably adapted. NEP 2020 Chapter 6 extends the idea to all Socio-Economically Disadvantaged Groups (SEDGs).
examRelevance: Definition-level question; also central to KVS interview.

text: The teaching skill of 'set induction' refers to:
textHi: 'सेट इंडक्शन' (प्रस्तावना) शिक्षण कौशल का अर्थ है:

options.text: Summarising the lesson at the end
options.whyIncorrect: That is the skill of closure.

options.text: Preparing/motivating learners at the start of a lesson by linking to prior knowledge and arousing curiosity

options.whyIncorrect: Unrelated to the technical term.
Testing is an evaluation activity, not an introductory skill.

explanation: Set induction (introducing the lesson) creates readiness — through questions, a story, a real object, a demonstration or a problem — and links previous knowledge to the new topic. It corresponds to Herbart's 'Preparation' step.
